S82.01.note: Searched the Billing and Usage settings for a plan-name row; did not find one. The /api/me route named in Code was not located in this pass.

S82.02.note: The date row label depends on the plan's period-end kind; a Free account has no such row.
steps: Open Settings from the app menu.
Click Billing in the settings list.
Look for the row that starts with Renews on, Ends on, Trial ends on or Current period ends, and compare with Expected.

S82.03.note: A Free account sees only an Upgrade button in this card, not a meter.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage in the settings list.
Find the card titled Plan usage limits.
Look at the bars labelled Current session, This week and This billing period, and check each shows how much is used.
Compare with Expected.

S82.04.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
S82.04.note: The flagship cap appears as the Most capable models bar in Plan usage limits, and only when showFlagship is true.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to the card titled Where your usage went.
Find the table captioned By model and check each model row shows a request count and credits.
Compare with Expected.
S82.04.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By model

S82.05.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
S82.05.note: Empty rows are not shown; a zero-usage account may see no table.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Find the table captioned By product area and check it lists Chat, AGI Work, Deep Research, AGI Code and Browser.
Compare with Expected.
S82.05.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area

labels.text: of voice left at today's price

S82.06.note: The Voice row is an estimate from remaining credits, not a minutes-used counter.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In the Plan usage limits card, find the row labelled Voice.
Read the line that says About N minutes of voice left at today's price, or No voice left until a limit above resets.
Compare with Expected.
S82.06.where: Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits > Voice

S82.07.needs: a paid account that has generated images this month
S82.07.note: The row is hidden when the account has no image requests.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled This month.
Look for the row labelled Images, which appears only when there were image requests this month.
Compare with Expected.

S82.08.note: No video usage row was found on the Usage page. Searched UsageSection.tsx for Video; only a video_seconds key in a counts mapping and a VideoCostEstimate in the composer were found.

S82.09.needs: a paid account that has run Deep Research
S82.09.note: Usage is attributed to research when the work mode is research.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and check the By product area table.
Find the row Deep Research.
Compare its credits and request count with Expected.
S82.09.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area > Deep Research

S82.10.needs: a paid account that has used coding or work mode
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went and open the By product area table.
Find the rows AGI Code and AGI Work.
Compare with Expected.
S82.10.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By product area > AGI Code and AGI Work

S82.11.note: No storage row was found on the Usage page. Searched UsageSection.tsx; only a knowledge-files route in apps/web/app/api/projects was found, which is not a settings screen.

S82.12.needs: a paid account with a response running
S82.12.note: The row only appears when the usage read returns a responses value; the card it sits in was not confirmed.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Look for the line labelled Responses running now.
Read the value shown as N of M at a time.
Compare with Expected.
Open Settings and click Usage.
Find the card titled Credit balances.
Read the rows Bonus credits and Purchased credits.
Compare with Expected.

labels.text: Past a plan limit, bonus credits go first

S82.14.needs: a paid account that has bought credits
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, read the Purchased credits row and the Bonus credits row.
Read the sentence starting Past a plan limit, bonus credits go first.
In Plan usage limits, check the included allowance bars, then compare with Expected.

S82.15.needs: a Free or paid account that has received a promotional or referral credit
S82.15.note: The copy promises a referral or promotion credit; whether a credit can be given to the tester depends on the account.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, find the row Bonus credits.
Read the amount and the line Next expiry with its date, or the note about referrals and promotions if there are none.
Compare with Expected.
S82.15.where: Settings > Usage > Credit balances > Bonus credits

S82.16.needs: a paid account with bonus or purchased credits
S82.16.note: Plan-reset timing appears in Plan usage limits; this item covers the credit rows only.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Credit balances, read the detail line under Bonus credits, which shows Next expiry with a date.
Read the detail line under Purchased credits.
Compare with Expected.

S82.17.note: The countdown text itself is built in formatUsageResetIn in packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts and was not read in full.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Plan usage limits, read the detail under Current session or This week.
Look for the Resets at or reset-in text next to each bar.
Compare with Expected.

S82.18.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
In Where your usage went, find the segmented control with Days, Weeks and Months.
Click Weeks, then Months, and watch the history table change.
Compare with Expected.
S82.18.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went

S82.19.needs: a paid account with usage inside a project
S82.19.note: Rows with no project in the workspace show the text Project not in this workspace.
steps: Open Settings and click Usage.
Scroll to Where your usage went.
Find the table captioned By project.
Compare with Expected.
S82.19.where: Settings > Usage > Where your usage went > By project

S82.20.needs: a paid account that has run a task
S82.20.note: The sidebar path to Tasks was not confirmed on screen; the label comes from project-icons.ts.
steps: Click Tasks in the sidebar.
Open any task from the list.
Find the section titled Cost and usage in the task panel.
Read the cost and token line, and compare with Expected.
S82.20.where: Sidebar > Tasks > open a task > Cost and usage

S82.22.note: The composer entry point for Deep Research was not verified; the estimate line is built in ResearchActivity.tsx.
steps: Choose Deep Research in the composer, type a question and do not send yet, or send it.
Look in the research activity panel for the line that starts with up to ~ and shows credits.
Compare the estimate with Expected.
S82.22.where: Chat composer > Deep Research > send a research request > Research activity

S82.23.needs: a paid account with a finished task
S82.23.note: The note Cost and token usage are recorded when this task settles appears while a task is still running.
steps: Click Tasks in the sidebar.
Open a task that has finished.
Find Cost and usage and read the cost line and the tokens line.
Compare with Expected.
S82.23.where: Sidebar > Tasks > open a finished task > Cost and usage

S82.24.needs: an account near a usage limit
S82.24.note: It shows only when the account is near a limit; it cannot be forced on a fresh account.
steps: Use an account that is close to a plan limit and open a chat.
Look above the composer for the usage warning banner.
Read the headline and compare with Expected.
Click Try later to dismiss, or Get more usage to upgrade.
S82.24.where: Chat > composer area > usage warning banner

S82.25.needs: an account at a usage limit
S82.25.note: The headline text is one of several per refusal reason; the card is rendered inline in the message list.
steps: Use an account that has reached a limit and send a chat message.
Look for the card in the chat that says a limit was reached.
Read the headline and the buttons, such as Buy credits or Upgrade.
Compare with Expected.
S82.25.where: Chat > send a message after a limit is reached > paywall card in the chat

S82.26.needs: an account blocked from one model
S82.26.note: The button text is a template with the model name; the label shown is the fixed prefix Switch to.
steps: Use an account that is blocked from the chosen model and send a message.
Look in the paywall card for a button starting Switch to followed by a model name.
Click it and check the chat now uses that model.
Compare with Expected.
S82.26.where: Chat > send a message after a limit is reached > paywall card > Switch to [model name]

labels.text: Upgrade or wait for the reset.

S82.27.needs: a Free account or an account at a usage limit
S82.27.note: Plan item ID S82.28 is absent from the plan file, so the range has six items (27, 29-33). The reset time text comes from paywallResetLabel in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx, whose exact wording I did not read. The wait button text for the free-capacity case is a constant (FREE_CAPACITY_RETRY_LABEL) I did not resolve, and it shows a countdown 'in ...'.
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan usage is used up (or wait for the limit to be hit in a chat).
Send a message in the chat composer.
Read the blocked card that appears in the chat message list.
Look for the sentence 'Upgrade or wait for the reset.' and any reset time shown under the headline; compare with Expected (wait option plus reset time, alongside paying).
S82.27.where: Chat > send a message while the plan's usage is used up, then read the blocked card

S82.29.needs: a paid account that can buy credits, at a usage limit
S82.29.note: The button appears only when the server's recovery action is top_up (apps/web/features/chat/lib/quotaPaywallSlot.ts). Settings > Billing also has a top-up panel, but its visible title was not confirmed.
steps: Reach a usage limit in chat with an account that can buy credits.
Read the blocked card and find the button 'Buy credits'.
Click 'Buy credits' and note the page or dialog that opens.
Compare with Expected: the purchase starts from where the limit was hit.
S82.29.where: Chat > send a message at a limit > blocked card > 'Buy credits'

S82.30.needs: a paid account with card billing (Stripe)
S82.30.note: The panel is shown only when the account can buy top-ups and billing is through Stripe (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx). The Settings nav label for Billing was not confirmed.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Billing section.
Scroll to the panel titled 'Auto-reload'.
Turn auto-reload on, set the threshold and save; a dialog titled 'Turn on auto-reload?' appears first.
Compare with Expected: the balance threshold and reload amount can be set and saved.

S82.31.needs: an owner account in a workspace
S82.31.note: The card is mounted inside WorkspaceUsageAnalytics (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceUsageAnalytics.tsx). The exact tab label that opens it was not confirmed.
steps: Sign in as the owner of a workspace and open the workspace console (nav title 'Workspace').
Open the usage analytics view that holds the card.
Find the card titled 'Monthly spend limit'.
Set a monthly cap and pick the enforcement option 'Block' (other option 'Notify'), then save.
Compare with Expected: once the cap is reached, managed usage stops.
S82.31.where: Workspace console > usage analytics > 'Monthly spend limit' card

S82.32.note: The Settings nav label for Usage was not found in the code (searched apps/web/features/settings for the 'Usage' label without a match), so the path opens from the Usage section itself.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Usage section.
Scroll to the buttons under the history chart.
Click 'Download CSV' and wait for the file to save.
Open the CSV and compare with Expected: a usage report file is downloaded.

S82.33.note: The form posts to /api/usage/discrepancy (apps/web/app/api/usage/discrepancy/route.ts). The success message after submit was not read.
steps: Open Settings and go to the Usage section.
Scroll to the buttons under the history chart and click 'Report a billing problem'.
Fill in the message and the period, then submit.
Compare with Expected: the report is sent and a confirmation or tracking result appears.
